title: Nobody Owns the c-File
setup: Both c-pawns are gone, and neither side has put a rook on the file they left behind. One move claims it.
hint: One file has no pawn of either color on it, and only one of your rooks has a clear path to reach it.
explanation:
## The Idea

The c-file has no pawn of either color on it, and neither side has put a rook there yet.

{{Rc1}} claims it first. The other rook cannot, because the queen on d1 is in the way. For now the rook stands behind its own knight on c3, but a knight can step aside in one move, and when it does the file belongs to the rook.

Rook first, queen behind: a queen at the head of a file is a target any minor piece can chase with tempo.
